newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain investigators seek clues to ship fire.
newsitem.headline: Spain investigators seek clues to ship fire.

text.p: Investigators began scouring the wreckage of a cargo ship at a dockyard in Valencia on Friday as families prepared to bury the 18 killed when a fiery explosion ripped through the vessel.

Special investigators from Madrid arrived to search for clues to what caused the explosion that set off a blaze on Thursday and engulfed the lower decks of a ship under construction in the Mediterranean port of Valencia.
While police believe a fuel leak in the engine room of the ship, named "Proof Spirit", could have triggered the explosion, investigators said they were making no assumptions.
"It could have been a spark produced by a leak. That is the assumption that everyone has made but we must take a lot of care in this investigation," said a local official.
Workers were trapped inside the engine room and other sections of the ship when the blaze filled the vessel with fumes. Others, their faces blackened by smoke, managed to flee.
Although the fire was small, the rescue operation was complicated by the fact that it was in the lower half of the ship's hold.
Two firemen were injured trying to control the blaze and some 10 workers were hurt, most only slightly.

Spain's Crown Prince Felipe and Princess Cristina attended some of the funerals in Valencia. Black flags hung from the balconies of local buildings and workers observed an hour of silence in memory of the victims.
